**LLM-COST-006 (MEDIUM)**
- The Bedrock invocation log group `/llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations` in us-east-1 has no retention setting, so every log event is kept forever.
- It is the only destination configured. There is no S3 destination, so there is no S3 lifecycle rule to check.
- The group is in the Standard class and was created 2026-10-15 at 21:48 UTC, which matches your mid-October start.
- Stored size is 124,494,376 bytes (about 124 MB). The stored-size figure can lag behind what has actually been ingested.
- Citation: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/Working-with-log-groups-and-streams.html

**How fast it grows**
- From 2026-10-15 to 2026-11-24 the group ingested 340,347,057 bytes (about 340 MB). Data arrived on 31 of those 41 days. The other 10 days have no datapoints, which I read as no traffic that day, not a measured zero.
- That averages about 8.3 MB per day, or roughly 3 GB per year at the same rate. Daily volume swings widely, from 0.1 MB up to about 37 MB. The peaks were 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-10, and 2026-11-24 is at about 28 MB so far today.
- Text and video data delivery are both turned on. Image and embedding delivery are off.

**Estimated cost**
All figures here are `(estimated)`. They use the CloudWatch Logs rates for us-east-1 from the Pricing API, read 2026-11-24: $0.03 per GB-month for storage and $0.50 per GB for ingestion.
- **Storage now:** 0.124 GB × $0.03 comes to about $0.004 per month `(estimated)`.
- **Storage after a year with no retention:** about 3 GB × $0.03 comes to about $0.09 per month `(estimated)`. It rises in a straight line the longer you keep everything.
- **Ingestion so far:** 0.34 GB × $0.50 comes to about $0.17 over the period `(estimated)`. This is a one-time charge per GB written, so retention doesn't change it. The ingestion price is the larger cost here.

So the growth is unbounded, but it's a few cents a month today. It matters more as a data-hygiene issue. The logs hold prompts and completions indefinitely, and a spike in traffic would grow them faster.

**Fix (you run it)**
```
aws logs put-retention-policy --log-group-name /llmops-demo/bedrock-invocations --retention-in-days <N> --region us-east-1
```
Choose N based on how long you need the logs for debugging or compliance. 30, 90 or 365 are common choices. Once a retention period is set, older events are expired by CloudWatch.

**What I didn't check**
- I didn't read Cost Explorer, so none of these figures is billed spend.
- The pricing record for storage is marked as the legacy version, so your actual bill may differ slightly.
- The Bedrock log-delivery success and failure metrics had no datapoints in the window. I take that to mean they weren't emitted, not that delivery is failing. The ingestion bytes show data is arriving.
- I only looked at us-east-1. I didn't run any Logs Insights queries on the log contents.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
